'''Sugiyama Shrine''' (杉山神社) is a {{ill|Shinto shrine|en|Shinto shrine|qid=Q845945|lt=shrine}} located in {{ill|Kanagawa Prefecture|en|Kanagawa Prefecture|qid=Q127513|lt=Kanagawa Prefecture}}, {{ill|Yokohama|en|Yokohama|qid=Q38283|lt=Yokohama City}}, {{ill|Kōhoku-ku, Yokohama|en|Kōhoku-ku, Yokohama|qid=Q1358965|lt=Kohoku Ward}}. It is the local shrine of former {{ill|Nitta|ja|新田村 (神奈川県)|lt=Nittamura|lt_ja=新田村|comment=changed title based on wikidata|qid=Q11503739}} Yoshida and is regarded as one of the prominent {{ill|Engishiki Jinmyōchō|ja|延喜式神名帳#論社|lt=Ronsya|lt_ja=論社|comment=changed title based on wikidata|qid=Q11064932}} of “{{ill|Sugiyama Shrine|ja|杉山神社}}”, the only former {{ill|Engishiki Jinmyōchō|ja|式内社|lt=Shikinaisha}} in Yokohama City and in old {{ill|Musashi Province|ar|محافظة موساشي|ca|Província de Musashi|ckb|پارێزگای موساشی|cs|Provincie Musaši|de|Provinz Musashi|eo|Provinco Musaŝi|es|Provincia de Musashi|fa|ولایت موساشی|fr|Province de Musashi|gl|Provincia de Musashi|hak|Musashi-koet|id|Provinsi Musashi|it|Musashi (provincia)|ja|武蔵国|ko|무사시국|lt|Musašio žemė|nl|Musashi (provincie)|pl|Prowincja Musashi|pt|Província de Musashi|ru|Мусаси (провинция)|simple|Musashi Province|sk|Musaši (provincia)|sr|Провинција Мусаши|th|แคว้นมูซาชิ|tr|Musashi (vilayet)|uk|Провінція Мусаші|vi|Musashi (tỉnh)|zh|武藏國|zh_min_nan|Musasi-kok|zh_yue|武藏國|qid=Q907398|lt=Musashi Province}}.

== History and Origins ==
A theory holds that a family which migrated from {{ill|Bōsō Peninsula|en|Bōsō Peninsula|qid=Q1022115|lt=Bōsō Peninsula}} enshrined its ancestors here<ref name="kamnavi-shinyoshida-sugiyama"/>. Although the founding period is unknown, the ''{{ill|Musashi Shikishiki-ki|ja|武蔵式社記}}'' states, “In Yoshida of Tsuzuki District, there is a small place called Sugiyama where the shrine is located,” while the manuscript compiled during the {{ill|Bunka period|ja|Bunka}}・{{ill|Bunsei|de|Bunsei|es|Bunsei|fa|بونسی (دوره)|fr|Ère Bunsei|ia|Bunsei|ja|文政|ko|분세이|ru|Бунсэй|simple|Bunsei|sr|Бунсеи|sv|Bunsei|tr|Bunsei|zh|文政|qid=Q1327119|lt=Bunsei period}} (1804–1829) – ''{{ill|Shinpen Musashi Fudoki-kō|ja|新編武蔵風土記稿|comment=changed title based on wikidata|qid=Q11503943}}'' – records details such as “An expanse of two dan and five u, north of the village, with a flight of several stone steps leading up to a torii {{ill|Torii|en|Torii|qid=Q234731|lt=Torii}} erected before the shrine: the main hall spans two ken by two and a half ken, and the haiden, facing south, spans three ken by two ken, with the sacred object immovable, belonging to the village’s Shofuku-ji {{ill|Bettō-ji|ja|別当寺}},”<ref name="kanagawa-jinjyacho-sugiyama (shinyoshida)"/> {{sfn|Newly Compiled Musashi Fudoki Manuscript, Yoshida Village}}. It is said that the shrine’s sacred treasures and historical records, which were once kept at Shofuku-ji, the temple acting as its Bettō-ji, were completely lost in a fire at that temple<ref name="tsugaruoukoku-sugiyama">[http://www18.ocn.ne.jp/~tugaru/sikinaisyasugiyama.html 武蔵国都筑郡唯一の式内社杉山神社を推理]（津軽古代王国）</ref>.

In {{ill|1908|en|1908|qid=Q2056|lt=1908}}, the shrine was Ranked among the local shrines in Yoshida Village of Tsuzuki District (which became Nittamura after the 1889 merger)<ref name="kanagawa-jinjyacho-sugiyoshida (shinyoshida)"/>.

== As a Ronsya of Shikinaisha ==
The theory that this shrine is a Shikinaisha existed even before the compilation of the ''Newly Compiled Musashi Fudoki Manuscript''. In works such as ''Historical Geography of Musashi Shikinaisha'' (first published in 1966 and revised in 1972 as ''Musashi no Koshā'') by {{ill|Saitō Yoshihiko|ja|斎藤義彦}}, a Shintoist of the Bakumatsu period, and local historian {{ill|Hishinuma Isamu|ja|菱沼勇}}<ref>[http://www6.plala.or.jp/guti/cemetery/PERSON/H/hishinuma_i.html Hishinuma Isamu]（歴史が眠る多磨霊園）</ref>, this view is considered persuasive.<ref>[http://www.okuraken.or.jp/depo/chiikijyouhou/kouhoku_rekishi_bunka/kouhoku52/ History and Culture of Kohoku Ward (Series: Our Town Kohoku, April 2003): No.52 Sugiyama Shrine – a Prominent Candidate]（公益財団法人 大倉精神文化研究所）</ref> Hishinuma Isamu bases his argument on several points: the existence of a minor place name “Sugiyama” in the area {{ill|koaza|ja|小字|lt=small name|lt_ja=小名|comment=changed title based on wikidata|qid=Q5327509}}, the fact that the Mori family – an old family in the region closely connected with the shrine – is said to have a history spanning over a thousand years according to oral tradition {{ill|Q11410744|ja|口伝|comment=changed title based on wikidata|qid=Q11410744}}, and the presence of “Asama Tsumuka”, an ancient tomb ({{ill|Kofun|ca|Kofun|cs|Kofun|da|Kofun|de|Kofun|eo|Kofun|es|Kofun|fa|کوفون|fi|Kofun|fr|Kofun|he|קופון (רוגם)|hr|Kofun (grobnica)|it|Kofun|ja|古墳|ko|고훈|my|ခိုဖွန်း|pl|Kofun (kurhan)|pt|Kofun|ru|Кофун (захоронение)|simple|Kofun|th|โคฟุง|tr|Kofun|uk|Кофун|zh|古墳|qid=Q1141225|lt=ancient tomb}}) on a hill (target: {{ill|Hill|en|Hill|qid=Q54050|lt=elevated area}}) behind the Mori family that attests to the former power of a local warlord {{ill|dogō|ja|土豪|comment=changed title based on wikidata|qid=Q11423883}}.<ref>[http://www.okuraken.or.jp/depo/chiikijyouhou/kouhoku_rekishi_bunka/kouhoku53/ History and Culture of Kohoku Ward (Series: Our Town Kohoku, May 2003): No.53 Sugiyama Shrine in the Ward]（公益財団法人 大倉精神文化研究所）</ref>. In addition, the local ''History of Kohoku Ward'' mentions that the “Mori” in the Mori family is derived from the “guardian forest” ({{ill|Chinju no Mori|en|Chinju no Mori|qid=Q11651158|lt=Sacred Grove}}) and that the family is locally reverenced as “Sugiyama-sama”. Moreover, nearby in Hayabuchi 3-chōme there exist the [[{{ill|North River Upper Ruins|ja|北川表の上遺跡}}]] and [[{{ill|Kitagawa Shell Mound|ja|北川貝塚|comment=changed title based on wikidata|qid=Q11401676}}]], and the ''Newly Compiled Musashi Fudoki Manuscript, Yoshida Village'' records that “a large shell mound existed in Yoshida Village of Tsuzuki District” {{sfn|Newly Compiled Musashi Fudoki Manuscript, Yoshida Village}}, with the local name “Shell Mound Field” still in use – evidence that archaeological sites in the area have long been known.<ref name="tsugaruoukoku-sugiyama"/> 

Like many other ronsya, the shrine is situated on an elevated spot along the {{ill|Tsurumi River|en|Tsurumi River|qid=Q7850292|lt=Tsurumi River}} of the {{ill|Drainage system (geomorphology)|en|Drainage system (geomorphology)|qid=Q285451|lt=water system}} ({{ill|Hayabuchi River|ja|早渕川|comment=changed title based on wikidata|qid=Q11511423}}).

== Other Information ==
The shrine does not have a resident Shinto priest ([[:en:Kannushi|Shinto Priest]]) and is concurrently served by [http://www.kanagawa-jinja.or.jp/search_dtl.php4?jid=359&cd=1203043&scd=000&npg=0 八幡社] located in {{ill|Hodogaya-ku, Yokohama|en|Hodogaya-ku, Yokohama|qid=Q1192964|lt=Hodogaya Ward}}, Setoketani Town.
